questions.q: What does the term 'Marketing' mean in relation to art works?
options: The physical creation of an artwork in a studio.
The business processes of promoting, selling, pricing, and distributing artworks to target customers.
The destruction of old or unsold artworks.
The act of buying art supplies from the market.
questions.explain: Marketing in art involves all the commercial activities aimed at getting an artwork from the artist's studio into the hands of willing buyers or collectors.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: Which of the following serves as an effective outlet for an artist to market and sell their craft works?
options: Abandoned buildings
Art galleries, craft shops, and hotels
Deep sea fishing ports
Underground tunnels
questions.explain: Art galleries, souvenir shops, craft stores, and the lobbies of major hotels serve as prime commercial outlets for artists to display and sell their work to tourists and art enthusiasts.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: An artist intending to mass-produce tie and dye fabrics for sale may require capital. Which of the following is a viable source of funding?
options: Stealing materials from a neighbor.
Using personal savings, securing bank loans, or winning art grants.
Selling the tools of the trade to competitors.
Waiting for money to grow on trees.
questions.explain: To fund large commercial art projects, artists commonly rely on personal savings, borrow from commercial banks, or apply for government or institutional art grants.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: In the contemporary art market, what is the fastest and most cost-effective way for young artists to advertise their works globally?
options: Pasting paper bills on neighborhood trees.
Paying a town crier to announce the artworks.
Using social media platforms and online portfolios.
Buying a billboard space in another country.
questions.explain: Digital marketing through social media and personal websites allows artists to reach a massive global audience cheaply and instantly.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: When an artist evaluates the monetary value of an artwork, which factors must critically be considered to avoid taking a loss?
options: The color of the buyer's clothes.
The cost of raw materials used and the time/labor invested.
The weather condition on the day it was painted.
The age of the paint tubes used.
questions.explain: Fair pricing of an artwork requires calculating the overhead cost of the materials used, evaluating the physical time/labor spent creating it, and adding a reasonable profit margin.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: What is the title of the professional intermediary whose main business is to connect artists with wealthy collectors, and who often earns a commission from selling artworks?
options: A museum curator
An art dealer
A factory manager
An art teacher
questions.explain: An art dealer (or art agent) buys and sells artworks, or acts as a broker between the artist and buyers, in exchange for a commission.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing

questions.q: Why is the marketing of art and crafts deemed highly important to the Nigerian economy?
options: It decreases the amount of imported goods people can buy.
It provides employment opportunities and generates income for practitioners.
It forces young people out of school.
It destroys indigenous culture.
questions.explain: The art and craft business is a robust sector that creates jobs, encourages entrepreneurship, boosts tourism, and brings in foreign exchange, thus supporting the broader economy.

questions.q: What financial term describes the surplus money an artist keeps from a sale after all production and marketing expenses have been subtracted?
options: Tax
Capital
Profit
Debt
questions.explain: Profit is the financial gain realized when the revenue generated from selling the artwork exceeds the total costs involved in making and marketing it.

questions.q: In sourcing funds for an art exhibition, a non-repayable sum of money provided by a government body or cultural institution is formally referred to as a:
options: Bank loan
Grant
Mortgage
Tax deduction
questions.explain: A grant is financial support awarded by an institution for specific projects (like art exhibitions) that, unlike a bank loan, does not have to be paid back.
